newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Long Huat buys stake in timber firm.
newsitem.headline: Long Huat buys stake in timber firm.

text.p: Malaysian timber firm Long Huat Group Bhd said on Tuesday it has agreed to acquire a 74.2 percent stake in a timber company and undertake logging activities in Laos.

The stake in Unicorn Timber Industries Bhd will be acquired for 271.13 million ringgit to be satisfied by a cash payment of 54.23 million ringgit and an issue of 32.86 million new Long Huat shares priced at 6.60 ringgit each, it said in a statement.
Long Huat said it would also undertake for Ace Plywood Sdn Bhd the extraction of submerged standing trees in the Nam Ngum Reservoir in Laos.

Long Huat will pay Ace Plywood 150 million ringgit under the sub-contract agreement. This will be satisfied by an issue of 4.55 million new Long Huat shares at 6.60 ringgit each and an cash payment of 120 million ringgit.
The timber concession in Nam Ngum Reservoir covers an area of about 50,000 hectares.
Long Huat said it has also proposed a two-for-one rights issue of 74.8 million shares at 4.70 ringgit a share.
Proceeds from the rights issue would be used to finance the cash payments for the acquisition and Laos venture, repay bank borrowings and for expansion programmes.

Long Huat has asked for the lifting of the suspension imposed on its shares on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange. The stock, suspended since April 3 at the company's request pending an announcement, was last traded at 11.50 ringgit.
